# Instructions for GitHub Copilot

`CLAUDE.md` at the repository root is the full reference (decisions, verified facts, open points):
read it before changing anything. VS Code does not guarantee that a linked file reaches every
request, so the essential rules are repeated here.

## Working rules (maintainer requirements)

- Only justified, verified answers: no inference, no assumption. Back every claim with a source
  (official doc, code, test, log, command output); say plainly when something is not verified.
  Show the reasoning first, then the answer. Answer in French.
- Check every change for security problems and personal data before proposing it (code, docs,
  commit messages): secrets, keys, tokens, signed URLs, the maintainer's name, e-mail, machine name,
  host paths and logs. The repository is public.
- Agent-facing files: any file written for an agent or loaded by one. At least: `CLAUDE.md`,
  `.claude/` (settings, rules, skills, commands, agents), `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.mcp.json`
  (project MCP servers, Claude Code doc "Project scope"); `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`;
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/`, `.github/prompts/`; `.vscode/`,
  `.devcontainer/`. Also any file imported (`@path` in a CLAUDE.md), linked or named as required
  reading by one of them.
- Keep the shared rules in sync: when a rule in this file, or in "Working rules" or
  "Change workflow" of `CLAUDE.md`, changes, update the other file in the same change.
- Reviews: when reviewing a PR or a diff that touches an agent-facing file, compare the shared
  rules of `CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and report any difference, and any
  new agent-facing file, import or link. Do not fix it yourself: propose the fix.
- Human review: Copilot code review reads the instructions from the PR's head branch, not from
  `main` (GitHub doc "Add repository instructions"). Any PR that touches an agent-facing file
  must be reviewed by the maintainer, not only by an assistant.

## Project rules

- `src/collector.js` must stay ES5 (Zabbix runs it in Duktape): no `let`, `const`, arrow
  functions or template strings.
- `templates/*.yaml` is generated by `tools/generate_templates.py`: never edit it by hand.
- Zabbix limits item scripts to 65,535 characters. The template embeds a comment-stripped copy of
  `src/collector.js`: keep new code compact and keep the comments in the source. The generator,
  `tools/validate_template.py` and `tests/embedded_script.test.js` fail above the limit; the
  current size is in CLAUDE.md ("Workflow").
- Only query Druid fields listed in `docs/intersight_metrics.json` (no inferred metric names).
- Run `tools/ci.sh` before proposing a commit; new behaviour gets a PASS/FAIL test.
- Never build a RegExp from a string in tests (CodeQL "Incomplete string escaping", PR #17 and #19):
  use plain text search (`indexOf` / `includes`).
- README, CONTRIBUTING and the guides of `docs/` exist in English and in French (`README.md` /
  `README-fr.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `CONTRIBUTING-fr.md`, `docs/UPGRADE_7.4.md` /
  `docs/UPGRADE_7.4_FR.md`, `docs/DEVCONTAINER_SECURITY.md` / `docs/DEVCONTAINER_SECURITE_FR.md`;
  each file links to the other language): every change is made in both languages, in the same PR.
  The CHANGELOG is in English only. `SECURITY.md` is a single file, English first, then a French
  section. Answers to the maintainer stay in French; code and comments in English.
- GitHub Actions: pin every action by full commit SHA, with the release in a comment.
- Base units only: store W, Wh, g, s, bps, B (data sizes), never kWh, kg, ms or KB (Grafana and
  external TSDBs read the stored value; Zabbix adds K/M/G prefixes on display only, base 2 for B).
  Convert source values to the base unit (ms -> s, throughput bytes -> bits, 0-1 ratios -> %),
  never a base-unit value to a prefixed unit. See "Units" in `CLAUDE.md`.
- A unit or scale change requires a new item key (new UUID, new series), with the old and new
  keys in the CHANGELOG: with the same key, the old history would be read in the new unit.
- Never commit Cisco pages (`cisco-docs/`, `Supported_Metrices.md`) or the Zabbix manual PDF
  (`docs/Zabbix_Documentation_*.pdf`): their terms do not allow redistribution.

## Dev container and security

- Git is read-only in the dev container: do not commit or push; the maintainer does it on the host. Do not
  produce patches or mbox files: edit the files, write the commit message to `.commit-msg.txt`
  (git-ignored) and give the maintainer the branch name ("Change workflow" in `CLAUDE.md`).
- Before editing, check that the working tree is clean (`git status`); if not, ask the maintainer.
  One change at a time: wait until the maintainer has committed before starting the next one.
- Check the commit message for security problems and personal data like any change.
- Never ask for `.git` to become writable or to commit from the container: a writable `.git`
  (`commondir`, hooks, config) lets the container run commands through git on the host.
- If an edit reports an error (for example `ENOENT`), check `git diff` before retrying: on this
  mount the write may have succeeded anyway, and a retry could apply it twice. Run `tools/ci.sh`
  only once all edits are done, never in parallel with them.
- Never read `params.json`, `*.pem`, `*.key` or `.env*` (credentials), by any means.
- Never call the Dev Containers credential relay (`/tmp/vscode-remote-containers-*.js`) or
  `.devcontainer/check-host-credentials.sh`: only the maintainer runs that check.
- Do not weaken the firewall, the read-only mounts, `no-new-privileges` or the system `PATH` of
  the entrypoint; see "Development environment" in `CLAUDE.md`.
